← SOLSTICE PROJECT NOTES

Oil-pan baffle quality standard

P4 owner update: the former V3 is the simplest baseline; radial and nested gated concepts are authorized nominal design exploration. Apply these standards in the main implementation and automated checks. Use independent review for the final candidate or a consequential unresolved question, rather than delegating routine quality ownership. Physical release stages and evidence protections remain applicable.

These design, modelling and production standards apply to this project's three Solstice GXP concepts. Use one evidence/gap register, the existing geometry checks and a short record of the relevant physical trials. A more complicated cage does not earn a higher quality rating merely by having more parts. The expanded design and production sections below implement the owner's request to account for missing variables, beyond the initial digital-delivery review.

Current design basis: A is the former V3 custom-gate baseline; B is the radial four-gate collector; C is the nested six-gate reservoir. Current nominal envelopes, inner/well footprints and BOM quantities are generated in delivery/CURRENT_DIMENSIONS.md. Their parameter source is src/design_parameters.py; the register records each design input and its evidence class. Only the published overall pan envelope is source-backed. Pan interior, cover, pickup/tube, placement and mounting interfaces remain proxy assumptions or unknowns. A's loose mounting blanks are undrilled, unpositioned stock, not a completed attachment design. V1 fixed dividers and V2 purchased-door proxies are historical alternatives.

Owner scope clarification, 2026-10-13: the active objective is digital reconstruction, design exploration and full virtual fitment against traceable scenarios. No physical pan measurement, mock-up, coupon, bench or engine test is required to complete this digital objective. A virtual fit pass is scoped to the modeled evidence and scenario surfaces only. Fabrication-release and engine-use checks below describe a separate future physical decision if the owner later asks to build or install a variant; they do not block digital work.

What acceptance means

StageAcceptable resultWhat remains outside that result
Digital prototypeReproducible, internally consistent concepts with understandable operation, honest evidence limits, clean cut profiles and usable review filesFit, supplier order acceptance, physical free movement, durability and oil control
Fabrication releaseA named variant has measured interfaces, resolved attachment and assembly, a toleranced fabrication drawing/BOM, supplier-approved processes and a successful representative hinge/joint couponApproval to install and run it in an engine
Engine-use acceptanceThe actual built unit passes installed clearance, retention, cleanliness, thermal/motion and service checks, followed by controlled oil-pressure validation against a defined baselineA universal starvation-prevention guarantee

Use PASS only for the stated check and saved evidence. HELD means required evidence or a deliverable is missing. FAIL means a demonstrated contradiction or failed check needs correction. A physical-stage hold does not prevent delivery of a clearly marked digital prototype.

Basis of a requirement

  • OWNER: the project brief: removable metal insert, retain the factory cover/pickup, compare three architectures, deliver editable CAD/cut files and honest limits.
  • SOURCE: an identified vehicle or supplier requirement, with URL/document revision and scope. Record conflicts; a rule for a different engine remains an analogy.
  • DESIGN: a proposed project engineering criterion. It needs its stated measurement/calculation/test; it is not an OEM specification or a proven safety threshold.
  • UNKNOWN: a value or behavior not yet established. Give it a tangible next evidence route (source retrieval, photo observation, bounded scenario or, for later physical work, measurement/test), its affected decision and the scope it limits. A warning by itself does not close it; an unresolved physical value need not block a digital study when it is kept explicit and modeled through scenarios.

Unless explicitly marked otherwise, engineering checks below are DESIGN criteria. Existing dimensions describe the current model, not minimum safe design values. Do not replace an unknown pressure, clearance, fatigue life or allowable load with a plausible-looking number.

Design standards

Service conditions and oil system

Before selecting the final architecture, complete one service-condition sheet. Record street/track use, tires and grip changes, intended acceleration/braking/cornering and combined transients, inclines, engine speed range, duration of sustained loading, start/stop and cold-start operation. Obtain conditions from the actual intended use or measured baseline logs. Do not assume a symmetric three-door layout handles all directions equally.

Register the model axes to the installed car and gravity vector: forward, left, up, engine tilt and pan installation angle. The current relieved side is model −Y only. For each sustained/transient case, sketch the expected effective-gravity direction and which region supplies the pickup. A static tilted liquid surface can help choose tests; it does not predict transient slosh, splash, entrained air or running-engine oil inventory.

Design variableRequired design treatmentEvidence that closes it
Oil specification and stateRecord actual oil grade/specification, intended temperature range, low/nominal/high permitted fill, dipstick calibration and engine-off versus running drain-back state. Consider cold high resistance and hot low resistance to leakage.Applicable engine/oil documentation plus measured test conditions; use the intended oil in decisive bench tests. Do not infer the approved fill from cross-engine sources.
Available oil and demandAccount for oil held in galleries/filter/head/turbo during operation, return location/rate and pickup demand over engine speed. Keep chamber volume, displaced metal volume and usable supplied oil separate.OEM/pump data where available and a bounded operating/bench measurement. A geometric cage-volume calculation alone is insufficient.
Refill pathsIdentify every intended path into the pickup region: each door, tube-side route, below/above walls and return passages. Check both steady supply and recovery after slosh at the worst measured fill.Flow-path drawing tied to measured pan; bench replenishment test under defined head/flow and oil state. Record flow/level recovery rather than only video.
Retention and bypassMap under-wall floor gaps, corner joints, cover gaps and the front relief. Identify which paths are deliberate drains and which defeat directional retention.Measured gap map, tolerance stack and comparative drain/retention test. Aperture area is a screening metric, not flow equivalence.
Pickup and air ingestionPreserve screen access and its original location. Resolve clearance to the full pickup/tube envelope and its movement, including doors, heads, mounts and weld beads. Avoid treating apparent immersion as proof against aeration/cavitation.Measured installed pickup envelope; physical trial fit and pressure/air-ingestion evidence under defined conditions. No numerical pickup clearance is adopted without applicable evidence.
Venting, deaeration and returnGive air a return/vent route as oil enters the cage; examine head/turbo return impingement, foam and whether an upper frame or retained cover traps air or redirects return into the screen.Section/flow sketch and observed bench behavior; running validation for behavior bench work cannot represent.
Windage and rotating partsRetain the intended OEM cover function; verify crank/rod and cover flex/motion envelopes rather than assuming static clearance to a photograph. Do not add an unverified scraper or raise the cover into a rotating envelope.Applicable assembly dimensions/measurements, correctly installed cover and dry-fit inspection through relevant engine positions.
Drainage and serviceOil and sediment must reach the drain; provide inspectable cleaning paths and removal access. Check whether gates can stick shut after storage or trap oil during service.Timed drain comparison at recorded temperature/orientation and post-drain inspection; document any revised service procedure explicitly.

Door mechanics and attachment

For V3, treat the door, two moving cheeks and welds as one moving assembly. Record mass/CG with material-density assumptions and include pin friction, viscous drag, seat adhesion, burrs, misalignment, end-head squeeze and wear. For V2, obtain the actual purchased hardware revision and instructions; proxy dimensions cannot close these checks.

The desired rest position is a design decision. The current custom gate has a nominal gravity-closing bias, while the cited commercial door intentionally rests slightly open. Stronger gravity closing may improve seating but raise the oil head/torque required to admit refill. Determine opening initiation, full travel, closing recovery and repeatability in the intended oil across temperature, orientation and representative pressure/head differences. Treat a measured initiation head or opening torque as a result to compare with available refill conditions, not an arbitrary target. Do not claim the animation's period is a physical response time.

No spring or damper is modelled or specified. Oil-film adhesion/stiction can delay opening, and the installed effective acceleration vector can reduce or reverse the nominal gravity bias. Include those conditions when choosing the rest position and test envelope. Do not add a spring/damper without a demonstrated need and a separate retention, temperature and response assessment.

Check the opening and closed stops as load paths, including leaf bending, stop impact, cheek bearing/tear-out, pin bending/wear and weld fatigue. They must retain their function after the qualified cycles and handling loads. Derive load cases from moving mass, measured vehicle/engine environment, oil loading and applicable impacts; choose material allowables and test margins with their source/justification. A cutting minimum does not establish structural strength.

Define a removable mounting scheme with explicit load paths into verified bosses. Include cage mass, retained/sloshing oil loads, vibration, thermal expansion mismatch with the aluminum pan, thin-sheet bending and fastener preload effects. Avoid contact/rattle or fretting against the casting and pickup. Demonstrate clamp-stack seating, adequate verified engagement without bottoming, access, compatible fasteners and positive retention. Account for welding access and insert/pan installation sequence; every permanently captured pin must be assemblable before its final head is formed.

Choosing between the alternatives

Keep the stock system as the baseline. Compare all variants under the same measured envelope and service conditions; do not score by appearance or door count.

OptionMain advantage to testMain uncertainty to resolveChoose only when
A — simple gated wellFewest current custom gate locations; shared hinge constructionOpen-bottom/front bypasses, thin-leaf distortion, custom pin retention and unmeasured mounting stackMeasured fit is feasible and common-condition refill/retention evidence justifies the gates.
B — radial collectorDiagonal gates and guide vanes test another supply-routing arrangementLarger vane envelope, more seams, corner hinge/weld access and refill behaviorMeasured fit, service access and bench tests support the added structure over A and stock.
C — nested reservoirOuter reservoir plus inner well tests staged bufferingLargest nested assembly; serial gates may restrict refill; more parts and service operationsMeasured fit and common-condition tests show useful staged behavior without restricting recovery or service.

The current evidence does not rank A/B/C on oil-control performance. Keep a brief decision record: evidence used, rejected alternative and unresolved risk. If the retained cover cannot support a variant's mounting stack, revise the carrier or scope before refining its hinges further.

Modelling standards

  1. One dimensional authority: keep nominal dimensions in the editable source and reconcile the design/evidence register, BOM and drawing against it. Store evidence class, datum and uncertainty for measured dimensions. Source dimensions need the document/revision and a feature-level interpretation; design additions such as corner radii must not be silently attributed to the supplier.
  2. Datums and registration: retain the current cage-bottom origin as the concept datum until an installed datum is measured. Then record the transform to the OEM mounting seats and car axes. Do not move geometry by eye to imply fit. Preserve local wall/pivot coordinate conventions and transformations so opening direction remains correct.
  3. Parametric edits: the shared input source is editable, but not every shape is safely driven by only WIDTH/LENGTH/HEIGHT. Hinge profiles, gate placements, P4 guide/rim geometry and pan proxies have dependent dimensions. After changing an input, run the full pinned checks, regenerate the register/summary, inspect the affected assemblies and cuts, and recheck clearances and stop contact. Prevent invalid combinations with focused checks; no general configuration framework is needed.
  4. Geometric scope: separate cut solids, joined subassemblies, purchased components, approximate envelopes and reference geometry by labels. Keep pins, weld envelopes and mounting features visible when evaluating clearance. Nominal butt contacts are weld locations, not modelled weld strength. Add weld-bead/access envelopes before physical release where they could interfere.
  5. Validation coverage: the D3–D5 checks are the digital baseline. Validate feature positions as well as outer bounds: holes, windows, seats, overlaps and sheet thickness. Recheck real supplier hardware when it replaces a proxy. Record intentional contacts and excluded objects explicitly rather than broadening exclusions to obtain a pass.
  6. Motion: mates must coincide with physical pin axes; moving rigid bodies keep their internal relationships. Sampled clearance is not a continuous sweep guarantee. Before physical release, bound minima/maximum intrusions between samples and include tolerance, thermal and deflection envelopes. Check door-to-door motion with differing angles, not only synchronized motion; independent corner combinations and swept envelopes matter when doors approach one another.
  7. Presentation motion: label historical V1 separation as an assembly illustration and V2 motion as an illustrative hardware proxy. Current A/B/C animations are arbitrary-phase kinematic demonstrations. Clips must reset without accumulated drift over loops and match closed/open reference geometry. Fixed structures and pins stay fixed during gate motion. Playback never certifies fluid response, mass/inertia, forces or opening time.
  8. Rebuild and custody: retain pinned tool versions, entry commands, source hashes, final STEP/DXF hashes and native metadata siblings. Distinguish presentation artifacts from production profiles. Run from the documented directory and fail visibly on export/check errors. Inspect regenerated outputs before replacing the reviewed delivery; keep evidence originals and a clearly identified previous candidate where requested.

Production standards

Release stages and the shop packet

Use four physical stages after digital concept review: measurement mock-up, representative process/hinge coupon, fitted bench prototype, and qualified engine-use unit. A coupon may be authorized with unresolved pan dimensions; label it accordingly so its successful manufacture is not mistaken for a released full kit. No stage authorizes an upload, purchase or vehicle change by itself.

For a selected full assembly, issue one revisioned packet with variant identity, dimensioned datum drawing, per-part material/stock specification and quantity, cut files, purchased hardware specification, weld map, assembly order, inspection characteristics and current open holds. Identify left/right or orientation-sensitive parts physically without adding loose labels or coatings in the sump. Record any approved substitution and assess its effect before use.

Production areaRequired controlAcceptance evidence
Material and hardwareTrace cage/leaf/pin/rivet stock to supplier grade, condition, thickness and lot/receipt; obtain certificates when needed for the selected allowables. Specify weld filler and cleaning/passivation route where applicable. Do not substitute unknown rod or decorative plated hardware.Stock identification, measured thickness, purchased part/revision and a brief compatibility record.
Environment/material compatibilityEvaluate stainless/aluminum interfaces, pin/cheek galling and wear, dissimilar-metal contact, moisture/contaminants, temperature cycling and oil/cleaner compatibility. Specify any isolation/treatment only after ensuring it cannot detach or degrade in the sump.Material/supplier evidence plus relevant coupon exposure and inspection. No unsupported lifetime or corrosion-immunity claim.
Laser files and stockUse nominal geometry without pre-applied kerf unless the chosen supplier explicitly requires it. Specify thickness independently of the DXF. Confirm minimum feature/ligament, hole position, cut taper, edge finish, flatness and material tolerances with the current supplier.D3/preflight plus supplier process confirmation at release and incoming measurements; exported profile validity alone is insufficient.
Edges and holesRemove dross, microtabs and sharp edges without eroding seat overlap, stop faces or narrow ligaments. Finish critical bores after relevant welding, using a fixture that preserves alignment; check pin fit at every cheek.Visual/tactile inspection, dimensional checks and assembled motion. Do not assume ordered deburring reaches small or thin components.
Welding and distortionSpecify joint location/extent, filler, fixture, tack/weld sequence and access. Qualify thin leaf-to-cheek attachment using intended stock and technique; control shrinkage/heat distortion. Keep welds and spatter out of hinge bearing/seat regions.Representative joined coupon, post-weld dimensions/flatness and appropriate joint inspection by the fabricator. Visual appearance alone is not fatigue proof.
Pin/rivet retentionSpecify pin stock length, final head geometry, usable free span and forming access; heads must remain physically captive without binding. For V2, define actual flange/wall grip and supplier-compatible solid-rivet installation.Finished dimensions, motion after heading/riveting and a justified retention proof/cycle test. No loose clip/nut reliance.
Mounts and fastenersFinalize boss coordinates, standoffs, thread/engagement, seating, preload/torque basis and locking/retention compatible with oil/temperature. Preserve OEM cover and pan sealing function.Trial-fit record, dimensioned stack and traceable torque/retention procedure. OEM torque is not automatically transferable to the changed stack.
Metrology and trial fitUse tools with resolution/uncertainty suitable for the proposed clearances; record instruments/datums. Inspect before welding, after welding and after pin/mount assembly. Include feeler/gauge checks or suitable non-damaging clearance transfer methods at hidden interfaces.As-built dimension sheet and photos referenced to actual part identity; registered OEM trial fit with cover/pickup installed.
CleanlinessRemove cutting, welding, finishing and marking residue. Use a compatible cleaning process; inspect inaccessible pockets and hinges, prevent recontamination and store clean/dry. Account for every temporary fixture item and piece of hardware.Documented final inspection and parts count; no visible loose particles, dross or trapped debris. Any quantitative cleanliness target needs an applicable source.
Service and traceabilityMark/record assembly revision, installation orientation, inspection points, removal order and any altered drain procedure. Avoid inaccessible wear areas or an assembly that cannot be safely removed.As-built photos/record, accessible inspection method and service instructions tied to the qualified configuration.

Tolerances and verification sequence

Prepare a short stack for each critical interface: pan-to-insert; cover-to-frame; floor-to-wall; pickup-to-door swept envelope; pin-to-bores; moving-to-fixed cheeks; head-to-fixed-cheeks; leaf-to-seat; and stop angle/contact. Include stock/profile error, jig location, weld shrinkage, pin/head variation, mounting distortion, thermal expansion and credible operating deflection. Use conservative bounds where statistical inputs are absent. Specify functional requirements first, then choose tolerances the process can achieve; do not assign every feature the CAD kernel precision.

Perform the cheapest decisive checks in this order:

  1. Measure/mock-up: identify the actual pan/cover/pickup, register axes/datums and test a full-size disposable mock-up including moving envelopes and mount reach. Stop if attachment or cover clearance cannot be resolved.
  2. Coupon: prove cutting/finishing, leaf-cheek joining, pin capture and stop construction. Measure cold/hot opening initiation, travel, return and leakage/refill behavior with stated oil conditions. Repeat after representative cycling and contamination/storage exposure appropriate to the service use; select exposure from an explicit use basis.
  3. Fitted bench assembly: inspect as-built clearances and mounting, independently actuate each gate, then test drain/refill/retention for the defined orientations and oil states. Include stuck-open/stuck-closed scenarios to understand consequences; do not run an engine with an intentionally failed gate.
  4. Durability and post-test inspection: apply justified thermal, vibration and repeated-door/stop loading to the fitted design or representative rig. Inspect for cracks, permanent deformation, fretting, wear, pin migration, lost preload and changed opening behavior. Set duration/load/acceptance margins from the intended life and evidence before the test; do not invent cycle counts after observing survival.
  5. Instrumented running comparison: define baseline, instrumentation calibration/location, sampling sufficient to capture pressure dips, synchronized RPM/oil temperature/load and acceleration/orientation, permitted oil fill and abort criteria. Repeat comparable baseline/modified conditions and examine pressure dips, recovery and adverse changes, not only average pressure. Start within a controlled bounded envelope; do not use public-road starvation testing. Post-test inspection and serviceability are part of the result.

A pass applies to the tested unit/revision/conditions. Changes to mounts, door material/mass, pin fit, stop geometry, oil paths or service envelope trigger the relevant requalification, not automatically every test. A pressure benefit under one maneuver is not a general engine-protection claim.

Source-backed numerical constraints

Numerical supplier/OEM requirements remain in the existing source registers: OEM pan evidence, fabrication research and cut-file preflight. These link the underlying GM pan specification, original-assembly service procedure, commercial-door mounting document, and SendCutSend specification feed. The retrieved feed age and conflicts remain material limitations. Revalidate external process requirements at actual release; this standards expansion performs no new web verification and adds no sourced numerical safety threshold.

P5 implementation status for D10: saved-solid Boolean checks cover five contexts, sampled closed/moving gate poses, and 1 mm-sampled vertical withdrawal with the cover removed. All concepts intersect the rising tube proxy after 4–7 mm when it is retained; all clear the vertical path in four contexts when the pickup/tube proxy is omitted as an assembly, while nested C intersects the narrowed-shell proxy at its installed pose. A new centroid-based gravity study computes signed gate torque per kg at every sampled 0–60° pose for seven total pan-frame directions: level plus six selected 15° effective-gravity tilts. All gates bias closed at level; some gates bias open under selected directions. This is static gravity on the saved stainless geometry, not oil response, friction, transient acceleration or an installed-car attitude measurement. The scene transform regression covers nominal 180° and a 37° translated test placement. Tool access, alternate tilted/shifted paths and stronger source-calibrated interior geometry remain open, so D10 is in progress. The same-part-number Vue service drawings improve qualitative topology context only; they do not close metric fit inputs.

Resolve differences between research proposals and the current A baseline explicitly. Earlier 35 mm cage depth, tab/slot proposal, ≥15 mm cheeks, 3.556 mm bores and stationary-cheek stop are not binding production dimensions. A instead uses 46 mm walls, butt joints, 14 mm cheeks, 3.6 mm bores and moving-arm-to-wall stops; the current assembly notes preserve the remaining coupon and strength qualification.

The A baseline's >1 mm sampled top gap is a project-selected digital screening criterion, not a source-backed minimum physical margin. Its nominal 1.58 mm result still needs the as-built/thermal/deflection stack before release.

Fabrication release checks — held until measured

  1. Fit register: identify the owner's installed pan and original cover. Record a common datum, five boss XY coordinates/seating heights/threads, bolt lengths and engagement, pickup screen/tube envelope, floor profile, cover relief, rotating/dipstick keepouts and removal path. Use measured values with uncertainty; photographs without calibration establish topology only.
  2. Oil paths: map closed-door refill, above/below-wall bypass, front tube relief, drain and sediment escape paths at measured oil levels. Select floor gap and enclosure position deliberately. An open bottom or tube relief cannot be assumed to retain a known oil volume.
  3. Attachment: replace unpositioned mounting stock with dimensioned mounts and an accessible, positively retained fastening scheme. Resolve the changed OEM clamp stack and cover seating. The recorded OEM 14 N·m figure applies to the original assembly; it is not blanket approval of modified hardware.
  4. Tolerance and joints: specify purchased pin/door revision and measured dimensions, sheet tolerances, hole finishing, axial float, weld locations and assembly order. Evaluate the full tolerance stack at the seat, pin/cheeks, stop, top frame and pickup. Nominal 1.58 mm clearance is not the available post-weld/hot clearance. Check continuous sweep or sufficiently bounded local extrema where close approaches occur.
  5. Representative coupon: build one actual leaf/cheek/pin assembly using intended stock, finishing, joining and end retention. Verify unrestricted inward motion, reverse seat, maximum stop, permanent pin captivity and no loose debris after assembly and representative hot-oil cycling. Establish usable clearances before cutting the full set. If a purchased-door alternative is reconsidered, test the exact hardware and specified mounting method instead of a proxy.
  6. Supplier and fabrication packet: confirm the chosen stock/process in the current ordering workflow, set quantities per chosen variant, and supply a revisioned drawing showing the unresolved details now resolved. Rebuild/recheck after changes. No supplier upload acceptance substitutes for the fit and mechanics checks above.

These are release conditions, not requests to purchase, upload or modify the pan now. A disposable measurement template or hinge coupon may be made as an explicitly limited experiment before full release.

Engine-use acceptance — physical evidence required

Inspect the completed unit in its actual pan with pickup and original cover installed. Record all clearances, free travel, pin and mount retention, weld condition, tool access and drain/service behavior. Clean and inspect for dross, abrasive residue, loose hardware and detached weld fragments. Repeat motion/retention checks after representative temperature and cycling exposure; determine the exposure conditions from the actual use case and materials.

Define pressure instrumentation, oil specification/fill/temperature, baseline conditions, operating envelope and abort thresholds before running comparative tests. Use applicable engine service limits and an accountable engine/oiling specialist where needed; do not invent a universal pressure threshold here. A normal engine run, a tilt demonstration or attractive animation alone cannot establish reduced starvation. Preserve results and inspect the unit after testing before expanding the operating envelope.

Keeping review proportionate

Re-run only affected checks after an edit, then one final artifact/manifest check. Geometry changes need the relevant geometry and motion checks; text-only corrections need link and claim consistency review. No scoring system, new service or elaborate approval hierarchy is required. Record the status and smallest next action in review/quality-assessment.md.

Use the measurement worksheet for missing inputs and the assessment gap register for consequences/priority. These standards cover the variables identified so far; they do not claim that every possible engine, manufacturing or service failure has been exhausted. Add a row when measured evidence exposes a new material condition, and retire a hold only with its closure evidence.

Current P4 digital release and publication checks

Run the pinned full check in STATUS.md after a source, dimensional catalogue, design-standard or publication change. It synchronizes the derivative register, rebuilds affected geometry, validates profile/BOM/motion results, generates current dimensions and media, then freezes review/candidate.json. Final release acceptance is independent and must identify that exact candidate SHA-256. Routine changes use focused deterministic checks; the full independent review remains at a frozen-candidate boundary or for a consequential unresolved question. Packaging verifies candidate membership, source/build/render receipts and a staged ZIP before replacing the current archive.

Full-profile checks compare STEP and DXF faces after XY translation only, including holes and all boundaries. Negative regressions cover shifted holes, changed windows, scaling, rotation, broken contours and units. Parameter checks reject impossible dimensions and changes to the calibrated hinge contour. This is nominal geometric validation, not manufacturing tolerance approval.

Current A/B/C nominal values and envelopes are generated in delivery/CURRENT_DIMENSIONS.md; the dimensional source is src/design_parameters.py, and the register retains datum, source, uncertainty and status for each input. Supplier nominals and display proxies never become measured installed coordinates. Each measurement record needs evidence and uncertainty. Actual fabrication/test results belong in a separate evidence record; preserve the blank coupon template.

The public site has a standalone check_dist.py so GitHub Actions can validate its links, current A/B/C view matrix and downloads without access to local CAD or research files. The local full site test additionally checks the curated archive against both BOMs. Website publication still consumes the frozen, accepted project candidate.

Render receipts bind STEP, kinematic sidecars, render commands and runtime versions to output hashes. Archive publication is atomic; external manifest/checksum files are derivative receipts and can be regenerated after interruption. Physical fit/performance holds apply only to a later physical release; they do not block the active digital modeling objective.
